title: Uniform Galois-partition bounds for open image and closed support
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebra. Work with module sheaves and their ordinary derived categories on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Constructible means locally constant with finitely generated stalks on a finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification], [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules], [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. A Galois partition $\mathcal P$ is a finite locally closed stratification of $X$ by connected reduced subschemes $S_i$, with a connected finite etale Galois covering $V_i\to S_i$ for each stratum. Here Galois means that a finite group acts on the cover and acts simply transitively on every geometric fibre. Let $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P}(A)$ be the class of sheaves whose restriction to each $S_i$ is a filtered colimit of sheaves obtained by finite successive extensions of locally constant $A$-module sheaves which become constant on $V_i$. No finite-generation condition is imposed in $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P}(A)$. Write $D^b_{\mathcal P}(X,A)$ for bounded complexes whose cohomology sheaves belong to this class. A dualizing complex on $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ means an object $Q$ of that category such that $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,Q)$ preserves it and every canonical evaluation-transpose map $M\to R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(M,Q),Q)$ is an isomorphism [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Suppose such a dualizing complex exists on $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be any closed immersion with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. On each of $U,Z$ use the same definitions of Galois partition, $\mathcal W$, boundedness, and constructibility. Write $Rj_*$ for derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and $Ri^!$ for the right derived functor of the left exact sheaf functor $F\mapsto i^*\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$; the arrow in this kernel is the restriction adjunction unit, and $i^*,j^*$ are inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then:

(1) For every Galois partition $\mathcal P_U$ of $U$ there exist a Galois partition $\mathcal Q_X$ of $X$ and $d_j\ge0$ such that $Rj_*$ sends $D^b_{\mathcal P_U}(U,A)$ into $D^b_{\mathcal Q_X}(X,A)$, and sends its intersection with $D^{\le n}$ into $D^{\le n+d_j}$ for every integer $n$. It sends bounded constructible complexes to bounded constructible complexes.

(2) For every Galois partition $\mathcal P$ of $X$ there exist Galois partitions $\mathcal P_Z$ of $Z$ and $\mathcal P_U$ of $U$ and $d_i\ge0$ such that $Ri^!$ sends $D^b_{\mathcal P}(X,A)$ into $D^b_{\mathcal P_Z}(Z,A)$ and its intersection with $D^{\le n}$ into $D^{\le n+d_i}$ for every integer $n$, while $j^*$ sends $D^b_{\mathcal P}(X,A)$ into $D^b_{\mathcal P_U}(U,A)$ and preserves all cohomological bounds. Both functors preserve bounded constructibility. All partitions and bounds here are independent of the complex to which the specified functor is applied. There is no invertibility assumption on $\ell$ on $X$, no excellence assumption, and no finite-generation assumption on the cohomology of objects of $D^b_{\mathcal P}$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.6.3, Proposition 7.6.5, Corollary 7.6.6 and Proposition 7.6.7, pp. 311-313; arbitrary Lambda-algebra coefficients in the application in Lemma 7.6.10. Corollary 7.6.6 concerns the closed immersion i (the word ouverte in its printed statement is a typo, as the complementary-open proof shows).

proof.text: The open subscheme $U$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. A finite Noetherian affine cover of $X$ pulls back to charts $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ on $Z$; an increasing ideal chain in $R/I$ lifts to one in $R$, so $Z$ is Noetherian as well. By [lem-per-galois-partition-exact-refinement], replace any input partition by a directed refinement; inclusion of the old class in the new holds for every coefficient algebra. Apply [lem-per-directed-galois-finite-tensor-generators] to that refinement whenever a finite list $C_a$ is used below. Refining input partitions enlarges the class on which we prove the assertion, so it suffices to establish the desired conclusions there.

We first record the restriction argument for $f:T\hookrightarrow S$, with $S,T$ Noetherian and $f$ open or closed. Fix a partition of $S$ and its finite list $C_a$ from Step 1. Their inverse images $f^*C_a$ are constructible prime-field sheaves by [prop-constructible-pullback]. Choose one Galois partition of $T$ trivializing them all by [lem-per-noetherian-constructible-galois-partition]. Inverse image is exact by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], preserves colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits, lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], and preserves arbitrary constant modules by [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module]. Hence $f^*(N_S\otimes_\Lambda C_a)=N_T\otimes_\Lambda f^*C_a$: choosing a $\Lambda$-basis of $N$ proves this on underlying sheaves by the coproduct comparison, and naturality in endomorphisms of $N$ makes it $A$-linear. On a trivializing cover this is constant with value $N^{\oplus e}$ for finite $e$. Apply exact inverse image to each finite filtration, each retract, and then the filtered colimit in the generator lemma. Closure in [lem-per-galois-partition-exact-refinement] gives a single output partition for the entire input class; its constructible subcategory gives constructibility for finite filtrations. Exactness also makes $H^q(f^*K)=f^*H^q(K)$, so restrictions preserve every cohomological bound. For an arbitrary constructible input, first choose a Galois partition by the same existence lemma.

source.place: 7.3.4; 7.4.3-7.4.6; restriction refinements in the proof of 7.6.6.

proof.text: Fix the dualizing complex $Q$ on $X$, and put $Q_U=j^*Q$ and $D_U=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,Q_U)$. Extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and its stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] gives $j^*j_!M=M$ and $i^*j_!M=0$. It preserves bounded constructibility: use the input strata in $U$ and any finite stratification of the complement with zero values. Restriction to the slice site, identified by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open], commutes with derived internal Hom by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Thus $D_UM=j^*D_X(j_!M)$ is bounded constructible for bounded constructible $M$. This comparison also identifies $j^*(\eta_{j_!M})$ with $\eta_M$: in the Hom-complex definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], restriction leaves the evaluation $(\varphi,m)\mapsto\varphi(m)$, the Koszul symmetry and its transpose unchanged. Consequently the latter map is an isomorphism by the hypothesis on $Q$. This proves that the particular $Q_U=j^*Q$ is dualizing, including its canonical biduality maps.

source.place: 7.6.3, p.311: the assertion that the restricted dualizing complex is dualizing, with the evaluation argument spelled out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-etale-internal-hom-localization] with $K=j_!L$, $N=Q$ and finite-prime-field coefficients, for $L$ bounded constructible on $U$. By Step 3 the first term is zero and the middle and third terms identify as $D_Xj_!L$ and $Rj_*D_UL$. The cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] therefore makes the second arrow an isomorphism. Put $L=D_UM$ and use biduality from Step 3 to get $Rj_*M\cong D_Xj_!D_UM$. Every object on the right is bounded constructible. This proves the prime-field finiteness assertion of 7.6.3 without a dimension bound or invertibility hypothesis.

source.place: 7.6.3, p.311; the internal-adjunction identity obtained from the existing localization triangle.

proof.text: Fix now the input partition on $U$ and its finite prime-field list $C_1,\ldots,C_r$ from Step 1. By Step 4 each $Rj_*C_a$ is bounded constructible. Choose $d\ge0$ with $R^qj_*C_a=0$ for every $q>d$ and every $a$. The finite collection of all nonzero $R^qj_*C_a$ admits one trivializing Galois partition $\mathcal Q$ of $X$ by [lem-per-noetherian-constructible-galois-partition]. Negative higher images vanish because a sheaf has an injective resolution in nonnegative degrees and direct image is applied termwise [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. If the list is empty, take $d=0$ and any Galois partition of $X$. These choices involve only the input partition, the morphism, and the finite list, never the sheaf to which the functor will be applied.

source.place: 7.6.5, p.312: the finite family of prime-field simple constituents and their images.

proof.text: For any $A$-module $N$ and prime-field sheaf $C$, there is a natural $A$-linear comparison $N_X\otimes_\Lambda R^qj_*C\to R^qj_*(N_U\otimes_\Lambda C)$. For each $n\in N$ it is induced by $C\to N_U\otimes C$, $c\mapsto n\otimes c$, and additivity makes these maps balanced and hence defines the sheaf tensor map. Choose a $\Lambda$-basis of $N$. Both tensors become coproducts indexed by that basis. A coproduct is the filtered colimit of its finite subsums, and [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit] makes $R^qj_*$ preserve that colimit; finite sums are preserved by additivity. For comparing coefficients, [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies both module higher images with the higher image of the same underlying abelian sheaf, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] computes their coproducts there. Thus the displayed comparison is an isomorphism. Its construction commutes with multiplication by each $a\in A$, so the isomorphism is $A$-linear, independent of the chosen basis. The continuity hypothesis holds since an open immersion into a Noetherian scheme is qcqs, and every sheaf here is killed by $\ell$.

source.place: 7.6.7, pp.312-313, prime-field tensor comparison (also 10.2.1); here the sheaf-degree case is the explicit basis-and-colimit calculation.

proof.text: For $C=C_a$, Step 6 and Step 5 show that $R^qj_*(N_U\otimes C_a)$ is zero for $q>d$ and belongs to $\mathcal W_{\mathcal Q}(A)$ for every $q$: on each chosen covering it is constant with value a finite direct sum of $N$. It is constructible when $N$ is $A$-finite. The constant tensor identification is the map on pure tensors; its stalks are the usual module tensor isomorphism by [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] and clause (1) of [lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension], and [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] detects the isomorphism. Additivity preserves retracts. For a short exact sequence of input sheaves, the derived long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] writes each middle $R^qj_*$ as an extension of a cokernel by a kernel of images of the two ends. The exact, extension-closed categories in [lem-per-galois-partition-exact-refinement] therefore retain both membership and the bound $d$, and retain constructibility for finite filtrations. Apply the finite tensor filtrations of [lem-per-directed-galois-finite-tensor-generators]. It follows that these three conclusions hold for every constructible input in the fixed partition class.

source.place: 7.6.5 and 7.6.7, pp.312-313: finite devissage, retaining A-constructibility via 7.4.6.

proof.text: Every input sheaf in $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P_U}(A)$ is a filtered colimit of constructible subobjects of the refined class by [lem-per-directed-galois-finite-tensor-generators]. Its higher direct images are the colimits of theirs: apply [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit] to the underlying torsion sheaves and [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] to retain module structures. Filtered-colimit closure in [lem-per-galois-partition-exact-refinement] then keeps the same $\mathcal Q$ and vanishing bound $d$. This is precisely where arbitrary, possibly infinitely generated, cohomology sheaves are allowed. No uniform bound on the lengths of their finite filtrations is required.

source.place: 7.6.5, last sentence, p.312; 7.4.3-7.4.6 for arbitrary Noetherian prime-field algebras.

proof.text: Let $K$ have cohomology in $[a,b]$ in the specified input class. Canonical truncations [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology, lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] express it by finitely many triangles with terms $H^q(K)[-q]$, $a\le q\le b$. Derived direct image is triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. Each such term has image cohomology only in $[q,q+d]$ by Steps 7-8. The triangle cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] and the kernel, cokernel and extension closure in [lem-per-galois-partition-exact-refinement] give image in $D^b_{\mathcal Q}(X,A)$, with cohomology only in $[a,b+d]$. If $K\in D^{\le n}$ choose $b\le n$, proving $d_j=d$. For a bounded constructible $K$, choose one Galois partition for its finitely many cohomology sheaves by [lem-per-noetherian-constructible-galois-partition] and repeat the finite-filtration part of Step 7 and this truncation induction. It remains bounded constructible. This proves all of (1).

source.place: 7.6.4-7.6.5 and 7.6.7: passage from sheaves to bounded complexes by their finite canonical truncations.

proof.text: For (2), fix the input partition $\mathcal P$ on $X$. Step 2 with $f=j$ gives a partition $\mathcal P_U$ for $j^*K$, with unchanged bounds. Apply (1) to this partition to obtain $\mathcal Q_X$ and $d\ge0$ for $Rj_*j^*K$. By [lem-per-galois-partition-exact-refinement], choose a directed common refinement $\mathcal R_X$ of $\mathcal P$ and $\mathcal Q_X$; thus both $K$ and $Rj_*j^*K$ have cohomology in that single class. Step 2 with $f=i$ and input $\mathcal R_X$ supplies a single partition $\mathcal P_Z$ for both $i^*K$ and $i^*Rj_*j^*K$. All these choices depend only on the partitions and the fixed immersions. Constructibility of these objects follows from Step 2 and (1) when $K$ is constructible.

source.place: Proof of 7.6.6, p.312: successive refinements on U, X and Z.

proof.text:
For the coefficient ring $A$, apply [lem-per-etale-internal-hom-localization] with first argument $A_X[0]$ and second argument $K$. Internal Hom from the coefficient unit is the identity: in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] its Hom complex into a K-injective representative $I$ has degree $q$ equal to $I^q$. Constant inverse image identifies $i^*A_X=A_Z$ and $j^*A_X=A_U$ by [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module]. The resulting triangle is $i_*Ri^!K\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to(i_*Ri^!K)[1]$. Apply exact inverse image $i^*$ using [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and use $i^*i_*\cong1$ from [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization]. This yields precisely
$$Ri^!K\longrightarrow i^*K\longrightarrow i^*Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow(Ri^!K)[1].$$
The closed topos lemma applies to the actual small etale closed complement for any closed immersion, with arbitrary commutative constant coefficients; there is no finite-ring restriction.

source.place: 7.6.6, displayed triangle, p.312, derived from the existing ordinary-etale internal-Hom localization lemma.

proof.text: Put $B=i^*K$ and $C=i^*Rj_*j^*K$. By Step 10 both are bounded in the one partition $\mathcal P_Z$. In the exact cohomology sequence of Step 11, each $H^q(Ri^!K)$ is an extension of $\operatorname{coker}(H^{q-1}B\to H^{q-1}C)$ by $\ker(H^qB\to H^qC)$ [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. These lie in $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P_Z}(A)$ by [lem-per-galois-partition-exact-refinement], as does their extension; the same assertion for its constructible subcategory proves constructibility. If $K$ is supported cohomologically in $[a,n]$, Step 9 gives $B$ in $[a,n]$ and $C$ in $[a,n+d]$. This sequence gives $Ri^!K$ in $[a,n+d+1]$. Thus take $d_i=d+1$. This proves (2), together with the exact restriction assertion of Step 2. If $U$ or $Z$ is empty the same argument uses the empty partition and zero sheaves; identity immersions satisfy the assertions with bound zero (the possibly larger displayed bounds remain valid).

source.place: 7.6.6, p.312: the bound c=c\prime+1 and the localization devissage; arbitrary coefficients as in 7.6.7.
